record_type: INVESTIGATION — RESOLVES the residuals, and CORRECTS a prior conclusion

CORRECTION_TO_MEGA_NHPLUS_DEFINITIVE_CEN.claim_made_earlier: MEGA's displayed folder sizes are NOT additive. Per-folder stated figures are unusable as a verification check; only the root total reconciles.
CORRECTION_TO_MEGA_NHPLUS_DEFINITIVE_CEN.VERDICT: THAT CLAIM WAS WRONG. MEGA's folder and year figures ARE additive, to within 0.01 GB.

evidence.nested_june_july_2024: 11.13 + 5.31 = 16.44 GB, matching the stated '6. June & July 2024' of 16.44 GB exactly

CORRECTION_TO_MEGA_NHPLUS_DEFINITIVE_CEN.how_the_wrong_claim_was_reached: I compared a sum of ROUNDED PER-FILE values against MEGA's EXACT folder figure, found 2024 measuring 3.51 GB high, tested for double-counting (correctly found zero), and concluded the discrepancy had to be MEGA's. The error was assuming my per-file values were exact. They are not.
CORRECTION_TO_MEGA_NHPLUS_DEFINITIVE_CEN.why_double_counting_was_the_wrong_hypoth: Because 2024 was HIGH, not low. A missing-file defect makes a sum SMALLER. Only rounding can make it larger.

ACTUAL_ROOT_CAUSE.finding: MEGA ROUNDS EVERY DISPLAYED FILE SIZE TO A WHOLE UNIT.

proof.interpretation: No file anywhere in the share displays a fractional GB or MB. Every one is an integer. Values present are only 1-4 GB, which is exactly what integer-rounding produces for a population of recorded calls in that range.

ACTUAL_ROOT_CAUSE.consequence: Summing per-file sizes inherits rounding noise that can run either way and can reach ~3.5 GB across a year. This produced the apparent 2022 -1.93, 2023 -0.48 and 2024 +3.51 residuals, and it is why they did not behave like a missing-data signature.
ACTUAL_ROOT_CAUSE.error_bound: Each GB-rounded file carries up to 0.5 GB of error. With ~30 large files per year the annual drift can reach ~3.5 GB in either direction - matching the observed spread precisely.

virtualised_grid.status: REAL and the reason the corpus grew
virtualised_grid.evidence: 2025-Feb 36 -> 66 rows (+83%), 2025-Jan 36 -> 51. Scroll-to-bottom REDUCED the visible count, proving un-mounting.
virtualised_grid.effect: files 621 -> 651, calls 203 -> 211, call hours 609.29 -> 630.74, and ~13 GB of real media that had never been seen.

rounding.status: REAL, and it is a MEASUREMENT-PRECISION limit rather than an enumeration defect
rounding.effect: per-file byte figures carry up to +/-0.5 GB each; annual sums drift up to ~3.5 GB
rounding.verdict: does not hide any file, but makes per-file sums unfit for reconciliation

TWO_DEFECTS_SINCE_CONFIRMED_REAL.note: These two are separable and both real. The first cost 30 files and 8 calls. The second cost nothing in data and everything in comparability.

WHAT_EACH_NUMBER_MAY_NOW_BE_USED_FOR.MEGA folder and year sizes: EXACT and additive. These are the authoritative byte figures and the correct basis for any reconciliation.
WHAT_EACH_NUMBER_MAY_NOW_BE_USED_FOR.MEGA per-file sizes (the `title` attribu: ORDER OF MAGNITUDE ONLY. Usable for ranking, for spotting a file that is obviously large, and for planning disk. NOT usable for reconciliation to better than about +/-1%.
WHAT_EACH_NUMBER_MAY_NOW_BE_USED_FOR.the 183.92 GB mp3-preferred download est: BUILT ON ROUNDED PER-FILE VALUES. Treat as 182-186 GB. Still decisively sufficient for a 500 GB disk, so the operational conclusion is unchanged - but the figure is not precise to the decimal shown.
WHAT_EACH_NUMBER_MAY_NOW_BE_USED_FOR.row counts and durations: UNAFFECTED. Rounding is in the size field only; durations are rendered separately and were never rounded.

RESOLUTION.2024_plus_3_51: Rounding. Not missing data, and not double-counting - tested and excluded.
RESOLUTION.root_gap_0_08: Rounding, which happened to cancel across 651 files. The agreement was luck, not proof.
RESOLUTION.files_missing_from_the_corpus: NONE. All 59 folders walked, 0 failed, 651 files enumerated.

DEFECTS_IN_THE_INVESTIGATION_SCRIPT_ITSE: The year-index ranges covered the MONTH folders, never the YEAR ROOT, so the listings carrying the stated sizes were never read - a clean zero.
Months were keyed by NAME alone. April exists in 2022 AND 2023, so both were summed into one bucket, producing plausible single numbers that were sums of two different months.
The unit lambda expected 'GB' while the regex captured only 'G' - a KeyError, which at least failed loudly rather than silently.
